New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s administration is actively debating whether the city has the legal power to detain Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu when he arrives for the U.N. General Assembly in September. The potential arrest remains under discussion despite questions over municipal authority, as reported by The New York Times. Mamdani, who said that was something he would consider on the campaign trail for mayor last year, revealed that he was currently consulting with the city’s Law Department to determine his options.

“I believe that prime minister Netanyahu belongs in The Hague,” Mamdani said, referring to the Dutch city that is home to the international criminal court, which issued an arrest warrant for Netanyahu in November 2024 over alleged war crimes in Gaza. “He’s a war criminal who has been charged by the international criminal court, and what you will find is that is an opinion that is held by many, purely because of what his actions have wrought over these past many years.” Mamdani said it was unclear to him whether he has the legal authority to order the New York police department (NYPD), which he oversees, to detain a foreign leader like Netanyahu. But he said he was in “an active conversation” with the city’s law department about the matter.

NYC mayor says in Times interview that’s he’s in ‘active conversation’ with city’s law department about the matter

New York City mayor Zohran Mamdani has said he was reviewing whether his administration could arrest Benjamin Netanyahu if as expected the Israeli prime minister visits the city for the UN general assembly in September.

Mamdani’s comments on Saturday’s episode of the New York Times’s the Interview podcast echoed ones he had made to the publication as he successfully ran for mayor last fall.

“I believe that prime minister Netanyahu belongs in The Hague,” Mamdani said, referring to the Dutch city that is home to the international criminal court, which issued an arrest warrant for Netanyahu in November 2024 over alleged war crimes in Gaza. “He’s a war criminal who has been charged by the international criminal court, and what you will find is that is an opinion that is held by many, purely because of what his actions have wrought over these past many years.”

Mamdani said it was unclear to him whether he has the legal authority to order the New York police department (NYPD), which he oversees, to detain a foreign leader like Netanyahu. But he said he was in “an active conversation” with the city’s law department about the matter.

“Whatever the law allows me to do in New York City, that’s what we will do,” Mamdani added. “But we won’t be writing our own laws to that end.”

The warrant which the ICC issued for the arrest of Netanyahu and other Israeli leaders accused them of war crimes and crimes against humanity in Gaza, including “starvation as a method of warfare, and … murder, persecution, and other inhumane acts”.

During his mayoral campaign, Mamdani characterized Israel’s military actions in Gaza as a genocide and Netanyahu as a war criminal, telling the New York Times in September that he would order NYPD to arrest Netanyahu in the event he ever set foot there. He also condemned the 7 October 2023 Hamas attacks on Israel as a “horrific war crime”.

The Times report back then cited legal experts who judged that having Netanyahu arrested “would be a practical impossibility” for Mamdani – and could bring him into direct conflict with the US’s federal government.

The US is not a party to the ICC and does not recognize its authority. And in February 2025, early in his presidency, Donald Trump ordered economic sanctions against the court, maintaining that it lacked jurisdiction over the US or Israel.

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s administration is actively debating whether the city has the legal power to detain Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu when he arrives for the U.N. General Assembly in September.

The potential arrest remains under discussion despite questions over municipal authority, as reported by The New York Times. Mamdani, who said that was something he would consider on the campaign trail for mayor last year, revealed that he was currently consulting with the city’s Law Department to determine his options.

“Whatever the law allows me to do in New York City, that’s what we will do, but we won’t be writing our own laws to that end,” Mamdani said during an interview on the NYT show The Interview.

“I believe that Prime Minister Netanyahu belongs in The Hague,” Mamdani told interviewer Lulu Garcia-Navarro, referencing the Netherlands city that hosts the International Court of Justice.

“He’s a war criminal who has been charged by the International Criminal Court. And what you will find is that is an opinion that is held by many, purely because of what his actions have wrought over these last many years.”

The stance marks a slight shift from Mamdani’s mayoral campaign last year, when he said he would directly order the New York Police Department to detain the Israeli leader. Mamdani stated at the time that the action would honor an arrest warrant issued by the International Criminal Court over Netanyahu’s execution of the war in Gaza, a conflict Mamdani and a United Nations commission have labeled a genocide.

Netanyahu dismissed the threats during a recent appearance with local radio host Sid Rosenberg, a frequent critic of the mayor. The prime minister rejected the remarks and countered by accusing Mamdani of harboring sympathy for Hamas, the militant group that launched the Oct. 7, 2023, attacks against Israel.

payload.title: New Yorkin pormestari selvittää Netanyahun pidättämisen laillisuutta
payload.summary: Zohran Mamdani neuvottelee kaupungin lakiosaston kanssa siitä, voisiko New York pidättää Benjamin Netanyahun tämän mahdollisen syyskuisen vierailun aikana.
payload.content:
New Yorkin pormestari Zohran Mamdani selvittää kaupungin lakiosaston kanssa, olisiko hänen hallinnollaan oikeus pidättää Israelin pääministeri Benjamin Netanyahu, jos tämä saapuu syyskuussa YK:n yleiskokoukseen. Mamdani on korostanut, ettei hänellä vielä ole selvyyttä kaupungin toimivallasta tai mahdollisuudesta määrätä New Yorkin poliisi ottamaan ulkomainen johtaja kiinni.

Kaupungin toimivalta vielä avoin

Mamdani kertoi lauantaina julkaistussa New York Timesin The Interview -podcastin jaksossa olevansa ”aktiivisessa keskustelussa” kaupungin lakiosaston kanssa. Juridisen arvioinnin kohteena on hänen mukaansa se, voiko kaupunki ottaa Netanyahun kiinni ja onko pormestarilla valta määrätä valvomansa New Yorkin poliisilaitos toteuttamaan pidätys. Mamdani sanoi itsekin, että oikeudellinen toimivalta ulkomaisen johtajan tapauksessa on hänelle epäselvä.

Kysymys voisi tulla ajankohtaiseksi syyskuussa, jolloin Netanyahun odotetaan vierailevan New Yorkissa YK:n yleiskokouksen vuoksi. Keskustelu kaupungin oikeudellisista vaihtoehdoista jatkuu, eikä Mamdani ilmoittanut haastattelussa lopullisesta ratkaisusta.

Asia ei tullut esiin ensimmäistä kertaa. Mamdani sanoi jo viime vuonna New Yorkin pormestarin vaalikampanjansa aikana, että hän harkitsisi Netanyahun pidättämistä. Hän voitti vaalit viime syksynä ja toisti nyt aiemman kantansa samalla, kun kaupungin lakiosasto arvioi käytännön toimivaltuuksia.

Mamdani vetoaa ICC:n pidätysmääräykseen

Mamdani sanoi uskovansa, että Netanyahu ”kuuluu Haagiin”. Hän vetosi kansainvälisen rikostuomioistuimen eli ICC:n marraskuussa 2024 antamaan pidätysmääräykseen, joka liittyy Gazassa epäiltyihin sotarikoksiin. Mamdani kutsui Israelin pääministeriä sotarikolliseksi ja sanoi näkemyksensä perustuvan siihen, mitä Netanyahun toimet ovat hänen mukaansa aiheuttaneet viime vuosina.

Mamdani katsoi, että saman näkemyksen jakavat monet muutkin. Hänen vahva arvionsa Netanyahusta ei kuitenkaan ratkaise sitä, mitä New Yorkin kunnallinen hallinto voi lain nojalla tehdä mahdollisen vierailun aikana.

Haastattelussa Mamdani ei sanonut, että ICC:n määräys antaisi hänelle suoraan vallan määrätä pidätyksestä. Hän jätti toimivaltakysymyksen avoimeksi ja kertoi selvittävänsä sitä kaupungin lakiosaston kanssa.

“I believe that prime minister Netanyahu belongs in The Hague,” Mamdani said, referring to the Dutch city that is home to the international criminal court, which issued an arrest warrant for Netanyahu in November 2024 over alleged war crimes in Gaza. “He’s a war criminal who has been charged by the international criminal court, and what you will find is that is an opinion that is held by many, purely because of what his actions have wrought over these past many years.” Mamdani said it was unclear to him whether he has the legal authority to order the New York police department (NYPD), which he oversees, to detain a foreign leader like Netanyahu. But he said he was in “an active conversation” with the city’s law department about the matter.
